cards.explanation: The answer is only as long as he lives. Paul says the law has authority over a man only as long as he lives (Romans 7:1). Once the man has died, that authority is finished. Paul is talking to people who know the law, so I think he trusts them to see where he's headed.

The answer is False. Paul says a married woman is bound to her husband as long as he lives, but if he dies, she is released from the law of marriage (Romans 7:2). The husband's death is what ends the binding. Paul sets up this picture so he can show something bigger in a few verses.

The answer is an adulteress, friends. In Paul's picture of a married woman, if she is joined to another man while her husband is still alive, she is called an adulteress (Romans 7:3). The timing is the whole point. Same woman, same other man, but everything depends on whether her husband is still living.

The answer is Him who was raised from the dead. Paul says they died to the law through the body of Christ, that they might belong to another, to Him who was raised from the dead (Romans 7:4). Think of the widow in Paul's picture, who is free to belong to someone new. Paul is telling his brothers they have that same kind of freedom, and it leads to Christ.
The answer is God, friends. Paul says they belong to the risen Christ in order that we might bear fruit to God (Romans 7:4). Notice he says "we," so he's counting himself in. The fruit goes to God.

The answer is the law, bakers. Paul says the sinful passions were aroused by the law (Romans 7:5). That's a surprising thing to say, and he's going to spend the next verses explaining it. He's not blaming the law itself, and he'll say so plainly.

The answer is True. Paul says the sinful passions were at work in our bodies, "…bearing fruit for death." (Romans 7:5) It's the opposite of the fruit he mentions in verse 4, the kind borne to God. Two kinds of fruit, friends, and they end up in very different places.

The answer is in the new way of the Spirit, bakers. Paul says we have been released from the law so that we serve in the new way of the Spirit (Romans 7:6). The service doesn't stop. What changes is the way it's done. I know a bit about getting pulled out of a dark junk drawer and handed a new job, and it's a good feeling.

The answer is False. Paul asks, "Is the law sin?" and answers, "Certainly not!" (Romans 7:7) You can almost hear him shutting that door before anyone walks through it, friends. He's about to explain what the law actually does.

The answer is coveting, bakers. Paul says he would not have been aware of coveting if the law had not said, "Do not covet." (Romans 7:7) It's the one sin he names here. The command named it, and then he knew.

The answer is True. Paul says, "For apart from the law, sin is dead." (Romans 7:8) He's describing how sin used the commandment to produce every kind of covetous desire in him. Sin found its opening through the commandment, friends.

The answer is False. Paul says, "So I discovered that the very commandment that was meant to bring life actually brought death." (Romans 7:10) It was meant to bring life, and it brought death to him. I think that's why he says he discovered it, like it caught him off guard.

The answer is that it deceived him, bakers. Paul says sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, deceived him and through the commandment put him to death (Romans 7:11). Notice who does the deceiving. It's sin, not the commandment.

The answer is holy, friends. After everything he said, Paul concludes, "So then, the law is holy…" (Romans 7:12) He keeps blaming sin, and he never blames the law. He's not backing off from the law at all.

The answer is so sin would be exposed as sin, bakers. Paul says it was in order that sin might be exposed as sin (Romans 7:13). He also says that through the commandment, sin might become utterly sinful. Sin gets shown for what it is, and the good commandment is not the one to blame.
